title: Family emergency calls using AI-cloned voices
summary: Callers pretend to be a relative or friend in trouble — an accident, arrest or stranded abroad — and ask for money fast. AI tools can clone a voice from a short audio clip, so the call may sound exactly like someone you know.
warning_signs: A familiar voice asking for money urgently
Being told not to tell other family members
Payment requested by wire transfer, cryptocurrency or gift cards
verification_steps: Hang up and call the person back on a number you already have for them
Agree a secret family code word to use in real emergencies

title: Fake "unpaid toll" text messages
summary: Texts claiming to be from a toll agency say you owe a small unpaid toll and will face late fees. The link leads to a fake site built to steal card details and personal information.
warning_signs: An unexpected text about a small unpaid toll
A threat of late fees or penalties
A link to pay that doesn't go to your toll agency's official site
verification_steps: Don't click the link or reply
Check your account on your toll agency's official website or app, typed in yourself
Forward the text to 7726 (SPAM) and delete it

title: "Phantom hacker" tech-support and bank-impersonation scams
summary: A pop-up or call claims your computer or bank account has been hacked. A fake tech-support agent, then a fake bank or government official, convinces you to move your savings to a "safe" account they control.
warning_signs: A pop-up or call telling you to phone a number about a virus or hack
Requests to install software or give remote access to your computer
Being told to move money to a "safe" or "protected" account
verification_steps: Don't call numbers shown in pop-ups; close the browser or restart the device
Never give remote access to someone who contacted you
Call your bank using the number on your card before moving any money

title: "Digital arrest" video-call scams (India)
summary: Callers pose as police, CBI, customs, ED or other officials and claim you are linked to a crime. They keep you on a video call, say you are under "digital arrest", and demand money to clear your name.
impersonated_entity: Police, CBI, NCB, customs, ED, RBI and courts
warning_signs: Claims that a parcel, SIM card or bank account in your name is linked to a crime
Being told to stay on a video call and not contact anyone
Demands for money to "verify" your funds or avoid arrest
verification_steps: Remember: police and investigating agencies do not arrest people over video calls
End the call and contact your local police station directly
Report at cybercrime.gov.in or call the 1930 helpline
